_comment: The one table that pins the compact numbers in the 'what Auto did' note,
autoSummary.ts, the note the editor shows when a user clicks Auto) and
`_auto_num` (seestack/edit/presets.py, the note an *unattended* job stamps on
the History Info panel for the same recipe). Both write the same clause —
'a ~0.12 sky, 4.7 px stars' — about the same picture, so a divergence reads as
the app measuring the image twice and getting two answers. Change the rule and
you must change this table, on both sides at once:
Cases are [input, expected]. The .xx5 rows are why the table exists: Python's
round() is half-to-even and JavaScript's Math.round() is half-up, so a
measured 0.125 sky read 'a ~0.12 sky' server-side and 'a ~0.13 sky' in the
editor. The Python side moved to floor(x + 0.5), which is what Math.round is —
the same fix _factor_label took in v0.332.1.
